title: Tencent Hunyuan Team Answers Questions on Reddit for 120 Minutes: No Deliberate Leaderboard Chasing; Next-Generation Model Scale Will Expand Significantly

content_html:
After rolling out Hy4 and Hy4flash in succession in November, Tencent began using a 120-minute open Q&A to respond to outside doubts that it had "fallen behind in AI." In the early hours of November 21, Tencent Chief AI Scientist and Hunyuan large-model lead Yao Shunyu appeared with team members on the tech community Reddit, answering nearly 100 questions in an AMA (Ask Me Anything) and laying out Hunyuan's R&D direction and cards for developers to see.

Parameter scale was the pain point asked about most. With ByteDance and Kimi both pushing toward trillion-parameter models, why is Hunyuan still stuck at around 700 billion? The team's response: Hy4 with 770B total parameters and Hy4flash with 224B are positioned more for general-purpose use rather than specializing in coding, and Hy4 still has a lot of room to improve, especially in post-training, where the team is pouring a lot of effort into large-scale reinforcement learning. The more critical information was hidden in one statement: Hunyuan is planning to train models with larger parameter scales, they believe in the Scaling Law and will keep investing, and the scale of the next-generation Hy models will "expand significantly further."

The small-model side has not been idle either. Facing questions about on-device scenarios, the team revealed a complete product line: a smaller Hy4-mini is already on the roadmap, a 24B to 31B dense model is being considered for development, a frontier Flash Lite is also on the way, and they will even make a smaller image model; for the video model, they asked outsiders to stay tuned. Their confidence comes from two already-validated judgments: "Hy3 and Hy4 have shown that solid smaller models can also beat larger models. More importantly, they cost less."

One user asked with a table of AGI development stages: Level 2 is the median level of a skilled adult, and Level 3 is the top 10% level—where does Hunyuan stand? The team's answer was neither humble nor exaggerated: Hy4 is currently at Level 2.5.

Among the technical-detail Q&A, the most weighty admission was about "overthinking." A user complained that Hy4 sometimes takes too long to reason; the team admitted this is a known issue: Hy4's goal is to raise intelligence as much as possible, and a too-long chain of thought (CoT) is the cost; the solution is to distill it into the more cost-effective Hy4flash, letting Flash use reinforcement learning to ensure a shorter chain of thought. They also did not shy away from saying that in post-training, the hardest behavior to improve is precisely "overthinking."

On R&D priorities, the team named two directions: creative writing and readability were listed as key areas for improvement, with room still to grow; and in their creed, data and evaluation are the most important tools for achieving AGI—data determines a model's capabilities, and evaluation guides the right direction. The team is also researching continual learning technology, allowing models to learn new tasks from continuous data streams without forgetting old knowledge, which they see as a very promising direction.

There was another telling shift: since Yao Shunyu took over, Hunyuan has given up the approach of chasing leaderboard rankings through benchmark scores. Some users noticed that Hunyuan did not publish results on common leaderboards such as GPQA Diamond and SWE Bench. The team explained that these benchmarks came out earlier and their scores have already saturated; what they show are newer, harder benchmarks like Agents'Last Exam. In model development, they will rely on better training data and diverse internal evaluations to address problems, "not deliberately gaming the leaderboard."

As for the most stinging question—given limited supply of advanced AI chips, can Hunyuan still catch up to the frontier? The team's answer was just one sentence, but it carried a fierce, all-in determination: they are squeezing existing resources to the extreme to catch up to the frontier level.
